stories.headline: Quad leaders strike critical minerals deals in Manila
body: Trump says the Quad, the US, India, Japan and Australia, has agreed deals to secure critical mineral supplies.
He said they aim to stop 'coercion by any single foreign supplier', without naming China.
Modi, Albanese and Japan's Sanae Takaichi met him in the Philippines.
stories.joke: Rare earths, now with fewer rare friends.
stories.vc: New mineral supply chains could bring mining and processing investment to India.

stories.headline: US loses its measles-free status after 26 years
body: The Pan American Health Organization has declared measles endemic again in the US, Bolivia and Mexico.
The same strain had spread nonstop in each country for at least 12 months.
The US is facing its biggest outbreak in more than three decades.
stories.vc: Outbreaks raise costs for hospitals, schools and employers.

stories.headline: Students keep up school blockades in Paris suburbs
body: Students and teachers in the suburbs of Paris are still blockading some schools.
They say little has improved in their classrooms since protests began in September.
Many joined a national strike on November 5, some in costumes.
stories.vc: Long school disruptions add pressure on France's education budget.

stories.headline: Sensex rises 427 points as banks lead a second day of gains
body: The Sensex rose 427 points to 82,532.19 and the Nifty closed at 25,387.40 on Tuesday.
Bank stocks led the gains.
Foreign buying and a sharp fall in crude oil prices helped.
stories.joke: Two green days. Don't say it out loud.
stories.vc: Cheaper oil cuts costs for Indian companies and helps the rupee.

stories.headline: Urban Company to pour ₹600 crore into its InstaHelp service
body: Urban Company will spend ₹600 crore from its ₹2,500 crore share sale on InstaHelp, its 10-minute house-help service.
InstaHelp lost ₹306 crore (adjusted) in the first half of FY27.
The money goes in over three years, mostly on worker pay guarantees and training.
stories.vc: Quick services are costly to scale; investors will watch the losses.

stories.headline: Karnataka bets on AI and chips at Bengaluru Tech Summit
body: CM D.K. Shivakumar opened the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit, themed 'AI and Beyond'.
He said Karnataka wants to be a global hub for AI, deep tech and chip-making.
The state earns two of every five dollars of India's software exports, about $173 billion.
stories.joke: Bengaluru: now with fewer potholes in its pitch decks.
stories.vc: Fresh state support could pull more chip and AI investment to Karnataka.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang will talk to Congress, and says he'd return as CEO
body: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will give interviews to three US House committees on December 1.
Nvidia's top lawyer follows on December 2.
Huang says he would be 'honored' to come back if the board wants him. (No new FT/Unhedged piece, so this is Al Jazeera's report.)
stories.vc: A Huang comeback, or not, is the biggest question for Nvidia shareholders.

stories.headline: Model ML raises $250M to automate junior bankers' work
body: London's Model ML raised $250 million at a $1.5 billion valuation.
Its AI agents build financial models, pitch decks and due-diligence reports.
General Atlantic and QED led the round. (Axios Pro Rata had nothing checkable, so this is TechCrunch's deal.)
stories.joke: Analysts, your all-nighters are being automated.
stories.vc: Banks could cut junior hiring as AI takes over grunt work.

stories.headline: Ex-Neuralink president's Science Corp raises $400M
body: Science Corporation, founded by Max Hodak, raised a $400 million Series D at a $3.5 billion valuation.
Its first product, PRIMA, is an implant that helps people with macular degeneration regain some sight.
It is approved in Europe and aims for the US next.
stories.joke: Seeing is believing, and now, funding.
stories.vc: Brain-tech is pulling in huge rounds from top investors.

stories.headline: Stratechery: Apple's new Mac controls don't solve AI agents
body: Ben Thompson says Apple doesn't ruin the Mac with its new permission rules.
But he argues they don't fix the problem of AI agents.
He asks whether Apple can think beyond apps, and reviews the iPhone Duo.
stories.vc: If agents replace apps, Apple's App Store business faces pressure.

stories.headline: SEC reportedly opens probe into Nvidia's disclosures
body: The SEC is investigating whether Nvidia misled investors, the Wall Street Journal reports.
It adds to probes linked to Jensen Huang's exit and alleged chip smuggling to China.
Nvidia reported earnings the same week. (No checkable Economist piece today, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: When it rains, it pours subpoenas.
stories.vc: Legal risk could weigh on Nvidia's share price for months.

stories.headline: Rebeca Grynspan could be the UN's first woman leader
body: Costa Rican diplomat Rebeca Grynspan, 70, keeps leading Security Council straw polls for UN secretary-general.
She would be the first woman and first Jewish person in the job.
But at least one veto stands in her way before the December 31 deadline.
stories.vc: A trade expert at the top could shift UN focus to development finance.

stories.headline: PIMCO's top equity trader leaves to back women in AI
body: Eden Simmer, PIMCO's head of global equity trading, is leaving to start UpLevel Impact Ventures.
The fund will back AI companies that help women reclaim time.
She wants women to be founders and investors in AI, not just users.
stories.joke: From trading desk to founding desk.
stories.vc: Women-focused AI funds are still rare, so new capital matters.

stories.headline: Andhra moves pregnant women to hospitals before a cyclone
body: Andhra Pradesh identified 3,478 pregnant women due to deliver between November 14 and 24.
It has already shifted 377 to nearby hospitals as a precaution.
282 of its 994 government health facilities are seen as vulnerable to the storm.
stories.vc: Planning ahead keeps mothers and newborns safe and avoids costly emergencies.

stories.headline: Mahe Government Hospital to get a day-care cancer centre
body: Puducherry plans a day-care cancer centre at Mahe Government Hospital, Lt Governor K. Kailashnathan said.
It will sit in a new block, which could open in February.
He also opened a new dialysis centre there.
stories.joke: Shorter trips for chemo. Small town, big upgrade.
stories.vc: Local cancer care saves patients long, costly journeys.

stories.headline: AIIMS Bhubaneswar opens three upgraded labs
body: AIIMS Bhubaneswar has opened upgraded newborn-screening, immunology and HPLC labs.
They aim to make specialised tests more accurate and easier to get.
The new platform can detect very low concentrations, the institute says.
stories.vc: Strong public labs cut patients' reliance on pricey private diagnostics.

stories.headline: Centre proposes 112 Ayushman treatments only at government hospitals
body: The Centre has proposed reserving 112 Ayushman Bharat treatment packages for government hospitals from December 1.
That adds 89 to the 23 already reserved.
States will decide whether to pull them from private hospitals.
stories.joke: Public hospitals: now with an exclusive menu.
stories.vc: Private hospitals could lose some scheme patients, while public ones get more.

stories.headline: Hudson River Trading's London trading income doubled in 2025
body: HRT's London company doubled its trading income to £106.6 million in 2025, its accounts show.
But profit before tax rose only about a tenth, to £89.3 million.
A £29.4 million drop in fees from related HRT companies explains much of the gap.
stories.joke: Doubled the trading, kept the modesty.
stories.vc: Big HFT firms are earning more from Europe's markets.

stories.headline: Talos, Marex, Broadridge enable after-hours trading of tokenised assets
body: The three firms will let institutions trade and finance tokenised securities outside normal market hours.
It supports DTCC's tokenisation service, live since October 28, covering US Treasuries, Russell 1000 stocks and big ETFs.
The first focus is financing tokenised Treasuries.
stories.joke: Markets never sleep. Now the paperwork doesn't either.
stories.vc: Round-the-clock trading opens new hours for fast traders and market makers.

stories.statLabel: drop in NSE index options premium (Aug)
stories.headline: Explainer: what is liquidity, and why it matters to HFT
body: Liquidity means how easily you can buy or sell without moving the price much.
After India cut weekly options, NSE's average daily index-options premium fell 43% in August to a four-year low.
Thinner markets can mean wider spreads, and higher costs for HFT firms like HRT's India arm.
stories.joke: Less water in the pool, harder to swim fast.
stories.vc: Lower liquidity makes trading costlier for everyone, not just HFT firms.

stories.headline: Norris says a wet Las Vegas GP would be 'scary'
body: Lando Norris says F1's current rain tyres won't work well at a low-downforce track like Las Vegas.
He hopes Pirelli brings much better wet tyres in 2027.
Brazil's wet qualifying was stopped for over an hour because of standing water.
stories.joke: Vegas odds on rain: please, no.
stories.vc: Wet-weather safety is a risk for F1's big-budget night race and its TV audience.
